content.title: About
content.content: Seedless mandarins are fresh citrus fruits that have been peeled and have no seeds. They feature a sweet‑tart flavor, juicy texture, and bright orange color. These mandarins are convenient to eat raw, add to salads, desserts, and beverages.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mandarins belong to the Rutaceae family and are close relatives of oranges and clementines.
Seedless varieties were bred for convenience and to reduce the risk of biting into hard seeds.
Mandarins contain more vitamin C than most other citrus fruits.
In Chinese culture mandarins symbolize luck and prosperity, especially during the New Year.
The harvest season in the Northern Hemisphere typically runs from November to January.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity, supports collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids help protect cells from oxidative stress and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: One mandarin provides about 40 kcal, making it a weight‑friendly option.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal heart function and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as skin itching or swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic fruit, rinse thoroughly to reduce any pesticide residue.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Seedless mandarins are perfect as a snack, in fruit salads, yogurt, smoothies, baked goods, or as a citrus component in sauces for fish and seafood.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store mandarins in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer in a sealed container or bag. At room temperature they keep up to 5 days; refrigerated they last up to 2 weeks. Keep them away from ethylene‑producing foods to slow ripening.
